analysis.one_liner: Bans paraquat, a weedkiller linked to Parkinson's disease, for all uses nationwide.
analysis.headline: The bill to ban paraquat never received a hearing or vote in either House committee it was sent to, and died when that Congress ended in January 2021.
analysis.plain_summary: Paraquat is a widely used herbicide that the bill's findings describe as acutely toxic and linked to Parkinson's disease. The bill would have immediately canceled its registration, banned residue on food, barred the sale of existing stock, and stopped the EPA from re-approving it. Over 70 other countries, including the European Union and China, already ban it [S3].
analysis.who_benefits: Farmworkers, growers, and rural residents who are exposed to paraquat by spraying, drift, or contaminated food, plus the general public; the bill's text singles out Parkinson's disease, and paraquat has already been banned in the EU, China, and dozens of other countries [S3].

how_it_helps.text: It immediately cancels EPA registration of every use of paraquat and bars the sale or use of existing stock, rather than waiting for the agency's multi-year review cycle [S2] [S3].
It revokes the legal tolerance that allows paraquat residue in or on food, removing it from the food supply [S2] [S3].
It permanently prohibits the EPA from reregistering paraquat, closing the door on re-approval [S3].

analysis.who_pays: Paraquat manufacturers lose their product's registration, and farmers lose a cheap, fast-acting herbicide for grassy weeds and would pay more for alternatives; some growers argue no drop-in replacement exists for certain orchard and row-crop uses.
analysis.who_pays_short: Paraquat makers and farmers who spray it

drawbacks.text: Farmers lose a low-cost herbicide for controlling grassy weeds, and replacing it would raise weed-control costs; for some uses there is no equally cheap substitute.

The bill legislatively declares paraquat causes unreasonable adverse effects and that the science is settled, bypassing the EPA's ongoing registration review, which critics would call a decision that belongs with the agency's scientists.
Banning existing stock immediately, with no phase-out period, would force growers and distributors to absorb disposal costs and find substitutes on short notice.

analysis.benefit_vs_cost: For people exposed to paraquat, the health benefit is large: the bill targeted a chemical its text calls a known neurotoxin linked to Parkinson's, and most of the world already bans it. The cost is real but limited — higher weed-control expenses for some growers and lost sales for one set of chemical manufacturers — and the immediate, no-phase-out design would have made the transition abrupt.

outcome.mechanism: It was sent to the House Agriculture and Energy and Commerce Committees in July 2019, split between two subcommittees, and neither committee ever held a hearing or vote on it, so it died when the Congress ended in January 2021 [S5].

narrative.text: Rep. Nydia Velazquez introduced the bill with two original cosponsors on July 17, 2019, and 15 House Democrats eventually signed on [S4] [S5].

The Speaker referred it to two committees the day it was introduced; it was then parked in the Environment and Climate Change subcommittee and the Biotechnology, Horticulture, and Research subcommittee [S5].
No further action was ever recorded — no markup, hearing, or floor vote — and the 116th Congress ended on January 3, 2021, killing the bill [S5] [S1].

outcome.who_came_out_ahead: Paraquat manufacturers and distributors kept their product's registration through the end of the Congress, and farmers who rely on it kept using it; the EPA's normal review cycle, which allows continued use in the meantime, remained the only path to a ban.

for.name: Rep. Nydia Velazquez
for.what_they_did: Introduced the bill to cancel paraquat's registration and ban its use and sale

against.name: House Agriculture Committee leadership
against.what_they_did: Never scheduled a markup, hearing, or vote on the bill in the 18 months after referral

against.name: House Energy and Commerce Committee leadership
against.what_they_did: Never scheduled action on the bill after referral

against.name: Paraquat manufacturers
against.role: Manufacturers and distributors of the targeted pesticide
against.what_they_did: Continued defending paraquat's safety and marketing it in the U.S. while most other countries had already banned it

sides.party_line_note: All three original sponsors and all 15 cosponsors were Democrats, and no Republican supported it — but since no committee or floor vote ever happened, the record shows no stated opposition by party [S3] [S4].

industries.note: The bill would have canceled their product's registration, banned existing stock, and barred reregistration, ending U.S. sales of a herbicide linked to Parkinson's. Their interest in keeping paraquat on the market runs directly against the bill's public-health purpose [S3].

industries.industry: Farmers and commercial growers who spray paraquat
industries.note: They would lose a cheap, fast-acting tool for grassy weed control and pay more for substitutes, but they are also among the most directly exposed to the chemical's health risks [S3].
Their competing weed-control products would gain the market paraquat is forced to surrender.
